newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoil falls up to $6 a tonne on futures, prem.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoil falls up to $6 a tonne on futures, prem.

text.p: NWE gas oil was knocked sharply lower by diving futures and slightly easier premiums.
May IPE gas oil last traded at $165.50 a tonne, down $5.50.
Traders said the futures contract had been looking for a sell-off after several days of climbing and this bearish tone was supported by weakness in U.S products.
Premiums were also a touch lower. After Thursday's spate of diesel deals premiums eased to May IPE +$11-13 cif and FOD and DIN premiums slipped about $1 apiece as well.
The Asian arb remains shut, even with the sharp drop, since Hin Leong, the main Singapore buyer, was now adopting a more moderate purchasing tone.
The Indian June tender for 315,000 tonnes, was less than expected, but could draw product away while South American interest has already taken material.
But, Indian material may be sourced from the Gulf and sustained tranatlantic demand was not anticipated.
Barge business was slowish, although an EN590 3kt parcel was sold at May IPE +$11.50 fob while heating was talked steady between flat and May IPE +$1 fob AR.
